author: Emily Brown
title: Nearly Half of Americans Say They’ve Gotten a Miraculous Answer to Prayer
summary: At a time when most research about faith focuses on declining church attendance or shrinking religious affiliation, the American Bible Society’s latest State of the Bible report points in a different direction: nearly half of Americans say they’ve personally experienced a miraculous answer to prayer. According to the organization’s State of the Bible USA 2026…
full_content:
At a time when most research about faith focuses on declining church attendance or shrinking religious affiliation, the American Bible Society’s latest State of the Bible report points in a different direction: nearly half of Americans say they’ve personally experienced a miraculous answer to prayer.

According to the organization’s State of the Bible USA 2026 survey, 48% of U.S. adults say God has answered one of their prayers in a miraculous way. Among practicing Christians, that number rises to roughly 90%.

The findings come from the American Bible Society’s 16th annual survey of U.S. adults, which tracks Americans’ beliefs and spiritual practices.

“These findings remind us that many Americans don’t simply believe God exists — they believe He is active in their lives,” Dr. John Plake, chief innovation officer at the American Bible Society and editor-in-chief of the State of the Bible series, said in the report.

The prayer findings also fit into a broader trend the organization has identified this year. Earlier chapters of the State of the Bible report found that about 9 million more Americans now fall into what the American Bible Society calls the “Movable Middle”: people who are curious about the Bible or open to engaging with it, even if they aren’t regular readers or active churchgoers.

Taken together, the findings suggest that while participation in organized religion has shifted in recent years, belief in God’s involvement in everyday life remains widespread. That’s especially notable given that the 48% figure represents the general U.S. population, not just people who identify as Christian.

One qualifying note: the survey doesn’t attempt to verify individual miracle claims. Instead, it measures what Americans say they’ve experienced.

But according to this year’s research, millions of Americans believe they’ve seen God answer a prayer in a way they can only describe as miraculous.
rewritten_title: Prayer Still Works — Half of Americans Say They've Experienced Miracles

title: Most U.S. adults have lived with a romantic partner they’re not married to by their early 40s
summary: Around three-quarters of Americans in their late 30s or early 40s have lived with a romantic partner they’re not married to at some point in their lives.
